::: {#sol-reversed-text-entropy}

To shorten the displays,
write $p(x_a, \ldots, x_b)$ for $\P(X_a = x_a, \ldots, X_b = x_b)$,
and $p(x_a \mid x_c, \ldots, x_d)$ for $\P(X_a = x_a \mid X_c = x_c, \ldots, X_d = x_d)$.
Each value's subscript says which variable takes it.

1. Listing the same variables in another order does not change their [joint entropy](#def-joint-entropy),
   because the reordered vector takes each reordered value with the same [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability),
   as in the proof of @cor-entropy-chain-rule-reversed.
   For the same reason,
   reordering the variables in a condition does not change a [conditional entropy](#def-conditional-entropy).
   The [chain rule](#thm-entropy-chain-rule-n), with the variables in their usual order, gives

   $$\entropyf{X_1, \ldots, X_n} = \sum_{t=1}^{n} \entropyf{X_t \mid X_1, \ldots, X_{t-1}}.$$

   With the variables listed as $X_n, X_{n-1}, \ldots, X_1$,
   the $i$th variable is $X_{n+1-i}$,
   and the variables before it are $X_n, \ldots, X_{n+2-i}$.
   So

   $$
   \begin{aligned}
   \entropyf{X_1, \ldots, X_n}
   &= \entropyf{X_n, \ldots, X_1} \\
   &= \sum_{i=1}^{n} \entropyf{X_{n+1-i} \mid X_n, \ldots, X_{n+2-i}} \\
   &= \sum_{t=1}^{n} \entropyf{X_t \mid X_n, \ldots, X_{t+1}} \\
   &= \sum_{t=1}^{n} \entropyf{X_t \mid X_{t+1}, \ldots, X_n}.
   \end{aligned}
   $$

   The first line reorders the joint entropy,
   the second is the chain rule,
   the third substitutes $t = n + 1 - i$,
   and the fourth reorders each condition.
   Both sums equal $\entropyf{X_1, \ldots, X_n}$,
   so they equal each other.

2. Fix $t$ with $N < t \le n$.
   For values $x_1, \ldots, x_{t-1}$ with $p(x_1, \ldots, x_{t-1}) > 0$,
   @def-entropy-given-value makes $\entropyf{X_t \mid X_1 = x_1, \ldots, X_{t-1} = x_{t-1}}$
   a [function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/functions.html#def-function) of the [conditional probability mass function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-cond-pmf) $p(\cdot \mid x_1, \ldots, x_{t-1})$ alone.
   The [$N$-gram model](#def-n-gram-model) makes that conditional probability mass function equal to $p(\cdot \mid x_{t-N+1}, \ldots, x_{t-1})$,
   so

   $$
   \entropyf{X_t \mid X_1 = x_1, \ldots, X_{t-1} = x_{t-1}}
   = \entropyf{X_t \mid X_{t-N+1} = x_{t-N+1}, \ldots, X_{t-1} = x_{t-1}}.
   $$

   Then

   $$
   \begin{aligned}
   \entropyf{X_t \mid X_1, \ldots, X_{t-1}}
   &= \sum_{x_1, \ldots, x_{t-1}} p(x_1, \ldots, x_{t-1}) \, \entropyf{X_t \mid X_1 = x_1, \ldots, X_{t-1} = x_{t-1}} \\
   &= \sum_{x_1, \ldots, x_{t-1}} p(x_1, \ldots, x_{t-1}) \, \entropyf{X_t \mid X_{t-N+1} = x_{t-N+1}, \ldots, X_{t-1} = x_{t-1}} \\
   &= \sum_{x_{t-N+1}, \ldots, x_{t-1}} p(x_{t-N+1}, \ldots, x_{t-1}) \, \entropyf{X_t \mid X_{t-N+1} = x_{t-N+1}, \ldots, X_{t-1} = x_{t-1}} \\
   &= \entropyf{X_t \mid X_{t-N+1}, \ldots, X_{t-1}}.
   \end{aligned}
   $$

   The first line is @thm-conditional-entropy-average,
   with $(X_1, \ldots, X_{t-1})$ as the conditioning variable.
   The second line uses the display above.
   The third line sums over $x_1, \ldots, x_{t-N}$ first:
   the second factor of each term does not depend on them,
   and summing $p(x_1, \ldots, x_{t-1})$ over them gives the [marginal](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-marginal) $p(x_{t-N+1}, \ldots, x_{t-1})$.
   The fourth line is @thm-conditional-entropy-average again.

   The two-variable [chain rule](#thm-entropy-chain-rule),
   with $(X_{t-N+1}, \ldots, X_{t-1})$ as its first variable and $X_t$ as its second,
   gives

   $$
   \entropyf{X_{t-N+1}, \ldots, X_t}
   = \entropyf{X_{t-N+1}, \ldots, X_{t-1}} + \entropyf{X_t \mid X_{t-N+1}, \ldots, X_{t-1}}.
   $$

   Subtracting $\entropyf{X_{t-N+1}, \ldots, X_{t-1}}$ from both sides gives

   $$
   \entropyf{X_t \mid X_{t-N+1}, \ldots, X_{t-1}}
   = \entropyf{X_{t-N+1}, \ldots, X_t} - \entropyf{X_{t-N+1}, \ldots, X_{t-1}}.
   $$

   An [entropy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-entropy) depends only on the [joint probability mass function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-joint-pmf).
   The [stationary sequence](#def-stationary-sequence) with shift $s = t - N$ gives
   $(X_{t-N+1}, \ldots, X_t)$ the same joint probability mass function as $(X_1, \ldots, X_N)$,
   and $(X_{t-N+1}, \ldots, X_{t-1})$ the same one as $(X_1, \ldots, X_{N-1})$.
   So

   $$
   \entropyf{X_t \mid X_1, \ldots, X_{t-1}}
   = \entropyf{X_1, \ldots, X_N} - \entropyf{X_1, \ldots, X_{N-1}}.
   $$

3. Fix $t$ with $1 \le t \le n - N + 1$.
   First, for each $s$ with $t + N \le s \le n$,
   the condition on $X_t, \ldots, X_{s-1}$ can be cut to the $N - 1$ variables just before $X_s$:
   for values with $p(x_t, \ldots, x_{s-1}) > 0$,

   $$
   \begin{aligned}
   p(x_s \mid x_t, \ldots, x_{s-1})
   &= \sum_{x_1, \ldots, x_{t-1}} p(x_1, \ldots, x_{t-1} \mid x_t, \ldots, x_{s-1}) \, p(x_s \mid x_1, \ldots, x_{s-1}) \\
   &= \sum_{x_1, \ldots, x_{t-1}} p(x_1, \ldots, x_{t-1} \mid x_t, \ldots, x_{s-1}) \, p(x_s \mid x_{s-N+1}, \ldots, x_{s-1}) \\
   &= p(x_s \mid x_{s-N+1}, \ldots, x_{s-1}) \sum_{x_1, \ldots, x_{t-1}} p(x_1, \ldots, x_{t-1} \mid x_t, \ldots, x_{s-1}) \\
   &= p(x_s \mid x_{s-N+1}, \ldots, x_{s-1}).
   \end{aligned}
   $$

   The first line is the [law of total probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#thm-total-prob-conditional), given $X_t, \ldots, X_{s-1}$.
   The second line is the [$N$-gram model](#def-n-gram-model), which applies because $s > N$.
   The third line takes the factor that does not depend on $x_1, \ldots, x_{t-1}$ out of the sum.
   The fourth line uses that a conditional probability mass function sums to $1$.
   Because $s - N + 1 \ge t + 1$,
   the same holds with $t + 1$ in place of $t$.

   Write $R$ for the product of these factors:

   $$R \eqdef \prod_{s=t+N}^{n} p(x_s \mid x_{s-N+1}, \ldots, x_{s-1}),$$

   which is $1$ when $n = t + N - 1$.
   No factor involves $x_t$, because each starts at $x_{s-N+1}$ with $s - N + 1 \ge t + 1$.
   Applying the [multiplication rule](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#thm-law-conditional-prob) once for each $s$ from $t + N$ to $n$,
   and then the cut above to each factor,
   gives

   $$
   \begin{aligned}
   p(x_t, \ldots, x_n)
   &= p(x_t, \ldots, x_{t+N-1}) \prod_{s=t+N}^{n} p(x_s \mid x_t, \ldots, x_{s-1}) \\
   &= p(x_t, \ldots, x_{t+N-1}) \, R.
   \end{aligned}
   $$

   The same two steps, starting from $x_{t+1}$, give

   $$
   \begin{aligned}
   p(x_{t+1}, \ldots, x_n)
   &= p(x_{t+1}, \ldots, x_{t+N-1}) \prod_{s=t+N}^{n} p(x_s \mid x_{t+1}, \ldots, x_{s-1}) \\
   &= p(x_{t+1}, \ldots, x_{t+N-1}) \, R.
   \end{aligned}
   $$

   The left side of the second display is positive by assumption,
   so $R > 0$ and $p(x_{t+1}, \ldots, x_{t+N-1}) > 0$.
   By the definition of [conditional probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-conditional-prob),

   $$
   \begin{aligned}
   p(x_t \mid x_{t+1}, \ldots, x_n)
   &= \frac{p(x_t, \ldots, x_n)}{p(x_{t+1}, \ldots, x_n)} \\
   &= \frac{p(x_t, \ldots, x_{t+N-1}) \, R}{p(x_{t+1}, \ldots, x_{t+N-1}) \, R} \\
   &= \frac{p(x_t, \ldots, x_{t+N-1})}{p(x_{t+1}, \ldots, x_{t+N-1})} \\
   &= p(x_t \mid x_{t+1}, \ldots, x_{t+N-1}).
   \end{aligned}
   $$

   The second line substitutes the two displays above,
   the third cancels $R$,
   and the fourth is the definition of conditional probability again.

4. Fix $t$ with $1 \le t \le n - N + 1$.
   The reasoning of part 2 carries over,
   with the later characters in place of the earlier ones
   and part 3 in place of the [$N$-gram model](#def-n-gram-model):

   $$
   \begin{aligned}
   \entropyf{X_t \mid X_{t+1}, \ldots, X_n}
   &= \sum_{x_{t+1}, \ldots, x_n} p(x_{t+1}, \ldots, x_n) \, \entropyf{X_t \mid X_{t+1} = x_{t+1}, \ldots, X_n = x_n} \\
   &= \sum_{x_{t+1}, \ldots, x_n} p(x_{t+1}, \ldots, x_n) \, \entropyf{X_t \mid X_{t+1} = x_{t+1}, \ldots, X_{t+N-1} = x_{t+N-1}} \\
   &= \sum_{x_{t+1}, \ldots, x_{t+N-1}} p(x_{t+1}, \ldots, x_{t+N-1}) \, \entropyf{X_t \mid X_{t+1} = x_{t+1}, \ldots, X_{t+N-1} = x_{t+N-1}} \\
   &= \entropyf{X_t \mid X_{t+1}, \ldots, X_{t+N-1}}.
   \end{aligned}
   $$

   The [chain rule](#thm-entropy-chain-rule), with $(X_{t+1}, \ldots, X_{t+N-1})$ as its first variable,
   then gives

   $$
   \entropyf{X_t \mid X_{t+1}, \ldots, X_{t+N-1}}
   = \entropyf{X_t, \ldots, X_{t+N-1}} - \entropyf{X_{t+1}, \ldots, X_{t+N-1}}.
   $$

   The [stationary sequence](#def-stationary-sequence) with shift $s = t - 1$ gives
   $(X_t, \ldots, X_{t+N-1})$ the same joint probability mass function as $(X_1, \ldots, X_N)$,
   and with shift $s = t$ it gives $(X_{t+1}, \ldots, X_{t+N-1})$ the same one as $(X_1, \ldots, X_{N-1})$.
   So

   $$
   \entropyf{X_t \mid X_{t+1}, \ldots, X_n}
   = \entropyf{X_1, \ldots, X_N} - \entropyf{X_1, \ldots, X_{N-1}}.
   $$

   Parts 2 and 4 give each character away from the ends of the text
   the same conditional entropy forward and backward,
   and part 1 gives the whole text the same total forward and backward.
   So the reversed text carries no more information per character than the text read forward.
   The two games tie only on average:
   in English, "q" is almost always followed by "u",
   but "u" is rarely preceded by "q",
   so a single guess can be easy one way and hard the other.

   People find the backward game harder because their guesses are worse, not because the text holds more information.
   A reader who guesses with a [probability mass function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-pmf) $q$
   in place of the true conditional probability mass function $p$
   spends $\crossentropyf{p}{q}$ [bits](#def-bit) per character on average,
   which exceeds $\entropyf{p}$ by $\kldivf{p}{q}$,
   by the [decomposition of cross-entropy](source-coding.qmd#thm-cross-entropy-decomposition).
   Years of reading forward make $q$ close to $p$ for forward guessing,
   and no such practice makes it close backward.

:::
